target.title: # PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)
target.body:
# PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)

## Summary

This PR introduces a stricter, policy-driven filesystem access layer (**PathGuard**) for OpenClaw agent filesystem tools, including local media (image/pdf) loaders.

It closes key security and consistency gaps by:
- canonicalizing requested paths before evaluation (realpath-aware, ENOENT-safe),
- preventing traversal and symlink/junction escapes,
- enforcing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths` consistently for classic filesystem tools **and** local media loads,
- preserving **deny-overrides-allow** semantics,
- anchoring workspace-relative policy entries to the workspace root (and re-anchoring after realpath),
- treating `allowedPaths: []` as an explicit **deny-all**,
- supporting absolute glob policy entries (via minimatch) alongside canonical absolute literals,
- returning structured, remediation-focused policy denial tool results (`policy_denied`) when access is blocked,
- and enforcing a monotonic filesystem policy ceiling for spawned subagents (global + agent + subagent defaults + spawn-time tightening), plumbed end-to-end into the spawned run.

**Important scope note:**

R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”

Remote URLs (`http(s)://`) and inline `data:` inputs are not treated as filesystem paths and are outside this layer.

---

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Security hardening
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [x] Tests

---

## Linked Issues

- Closes #39672
- Related #8719

---

## Problem Statement (What was wrong before)

Before this PR, filesystem tool enforcement had multiple gaps:

1) **Path canonicalization and symlink escape handling were fragmented**
- Traversal protections and “what path are we actually touching?” logic were spread across tools/flows.
- Non-existent paths (ENOENT) were tricky: naive realpath calls fail and can allow later-creation escapes.

2) **Policy matching was inconsistent**
- Absolute vs relative entries could be evaluated in different “path spaces”.
- Glob vs non-glob entries could diverge in behavior, especially when “roots” filtering was used as an approximation.

3) **Media tools could diverge from file tool policy**
- Local file references inside image/pdf flows could reopen outside-workspace reads if not enforced per resolved file.

4) **Sandbox and host flows lacked a unified enforcement story**
- Enforcement needed to be identical regardless of whether the run is sandboxed or host-based.

5) **Spawned subagents did not have a guaranteed filesystem policy ceiling**
- Subagents needed an explicit, monotonic ceiling that could not be loosened at spawn time.

---

## What Changed (Design + Implementation)

### 1) Core PathGuard enforcement (`src/security/path-guard.ts`)

PathGuard implements:

- **Canonical resolution for existing paths** via `fs.realpath`.
- **Nearest-existing-parent resolution** for ENOENT paths (prevents “create later via symlink” bypass).
- **Symlink/junction-aware comparisons** in canonical path space.
- **Deny precedence**: deny rules always override allow rules.
- **Workspace-only boundary**: `workspaceOnly` blocks outside-workspace access.
- **Relative entry anchoring**: workspace-relative policy entries are anchored to the workspace root, and re-anchored after realpath resolution.
- **Empty allowlists**: `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit deny-all.
- **Absolute policy entries**:
  - absolute **literals** are canonicalized before comparison,
  - absolute **globs** are supported (matched against canonical real paths) without attempting to realpath the pattern.
- **Glob detection** via `Minimatch(...).hasMagic()` (brace/extglob supported).

### 2) Filesystem tool integration (read/write/edit/apply_patch-style)

- Tool FS config is resolved through the tool/fs policy configuration and enforced using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`.
- Wrappers normalize args and run PathGuard checks on resolved paths.
- `apply_patch` is explicitly guarded by parsing patch hunks and enforcing FS policy on each patch target path (not just args.path/file_path).

### 3) Structured `policy_denied` tool result (model guidance)

When PathGuard denies access, tools return a structured tool result (instead of only throwing a raw error) that:
- states the restriction is system-enforced and cannot be bypassed,
- describes what the tool attempted to do,
- provides actionable remediation options,
- and explicitly points to config keys that can be changed to grant access.

This improves model behavior: fewer useless retries, more direct user remediation.

### 4) Media tool integration (image/pdf local paths)

Local media loads are now policy-checked on the resolved file path:
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.ts`

Key invariant:
- enforcement is per resolved path using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`, not via root-prefix approximations.

### 5) Sandbox behavior

For local media loads in sandbox mode:
- PathGuard runs in sandbox flows too,
- policy root uses `sandbox.root` when sandboxed,
- otherwise `workspaceDir` is used.

### 6) Subagent filesystem policy ceiling (spawn-time tightening + runtime enforcement)

Goal: spawned subagents must never receive broader filesystem access than the configured ceiling.

Policy sources (monotonic tightening):
- Global: `tools.fs`
- Per-agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- Subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- Sessions-spawn defaults/ceiling: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (applied when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`)
- Spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge semantics:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: enforced as a ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

Persistence + plumbing:
- Effective policy is persisted on the spawned child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) via `sessions.patch`.
- Gateway plumbs it into the child run as ingress field `toolFsPolicy`.
- Gateway session resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve `spawnedToolFsPolicy` (no widening after reset).
- Embedded runner passes it into tool construction.
- `createOpenClawCodingTools` accepts an `fsPolicy` override and uses it as the effective policy for that run.
- Nested spawns inherit the parent session’s `spawnedToolFsPolicy` ceiling before applying config/tool-call tightening.

---

## Configuration (for contributors)

### Filesystem policy knobs

- `tools.fs.workspaceOnly: boolean`
- `tools.fs.allowedPaths: string[] | undefined` (empty array means deny-all)
- `tools.fs.denyPaths: string[] | undefined`

Subagent ceiling:
- `tools.subagents.fs.{workspaceOnly, allowedPaths, denyPaths}`

Sessions-spawn defaults + spawn-time tightening:
- `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (config default ceiling/tightening)
- `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (tool arg tightening; can only further restrict)

Notes:
- Deny always wins.
- Relative entries are workspace-anchored.
- Policies are evaluated against canonicalized real paths.

---

## Explicit Non-Goals / Out of Scope

- Exec sandboxing is not implemented here.
  R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”
- No shell argument parsing.
- Remote source governance is out-of-scope.

---

## Implementation Notes (for contributors)

### Policy evaluation edge cases covered

- `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit **deny-all** (not “no restriction”).
- Relative literal entries are **re-anchored after realpath**: if a workspace-relative entry canonicalizes outside the workspace (e.g. it points at a symlink to an external dir), it **does not** match outside-workspace targets.
- Absolute glob entries support symlink-alias authoring by **canonicalizing the non-glob prefix** before matching.
  - When rebuilding the rewritten pattern, the implementation **normalizes slash joining** so root-anchored globs stay semantically equivalent (e.g. `"/**/*.pem"` must not become `"//**/*.pem"`).

### Tool behavior on denial (model guidance)

When a filesystem access is blocked by PathGuard, tools return a structured `policy_denied` result (English text + structured fields) so models:
- do not attempt “bypass retries”,
- clearly communicate what was attempted,
- present actionable remediation options,
- and point to config keys (`tools.fs.*`) for operators to change if access is intended.

### Subagent filesystem ceiling (monotonic tightening)

Effective subagent policy is computed as a ceiling and is monotonic (cannot be widened by spawn calls):
- global: `tools.fs`
- agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- sessions-spawn defaults: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`
- spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` / tool arg `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge intent:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

The effective ceiling is persisted on the child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) and forwarded into the embedded runner (`toolFsPolicy` → `createOpenClawCodingTools({ fsPolicy })`).

---

## Verification

- CI checks and tests pass (per latest runs).
- Added/maintained coverage ensuring `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` is applied as a default tightening when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`.
- Verified critical denial scenarios: traversal, symlink/junction escapes, ENOENT parent-walk, deny precedence, empty allowlist deny-all, sandbox media enforcement, apply_patch enforcement, and subagent ceiling propagation.
- Verified monotonic nested spawning: a tightened subagent cannot spawn a child with broader FS access (parent `spawnedToolFsPolicy` is inherited).
- Verified gateway resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve the spawned FS ceiling (no widening after reset).

---

## Reviewer / Contributor Notes (Do not regress these invariants)

- Do not replace per-path enforcement with root-prefix approximations for glob policies.
- Keep deny-overrides-allow.
- Keep relative policy entries anchored to workspace (including after realpath).
- Keep sandbox and host local-file enforcement aligned.
- Keep local filesystem policy and remote-source policy separate concepts.
- Keep subagent policy tightening monotonic (no privilege escalation vs ceiling).
- Remember: exec is outside this enforcement layer.

---

## Rollback / Recovery

- Disable restrictions by setting `workspaceOnly: false` and clearing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths`.
- No data migration required.

target.title: feat(agents): derive fallbacks from configured model catalog
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw only derives failover candidates from `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, so operators who keep multiple models in `agents.defaults.models` still have to duplicate that ordered list manually.
- Why it matters: if the configured primary becomes unavailable, the runtime stops at the primary unless the same catalog is copied into `fallbacks`, which is easy to miss and easy to drift.
- What changed: added an explicit opt-in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacksFromModels: true` that derives fallback candidates from `agents.defaults.models` in config order when explicit `fallbacks` are omitted.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this PR does not change existing fallback error classification, auth-profile rotation behavior, or the meaning of explicit `fallbacks` / `fallbacks: []`.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #60919
- Related #47434
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: the fallback resolver only consulted explicit fallback arrays (`fallbacksOverride` or `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`). `agents.defaults.models` remained allowlist/catalog-only, so keeping multiple configured models there did not influence failover.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no opt-in config path that said “use my configured model catalog as the fallback pool when I omit explicit fallbacks.”
- Contributing context (if known): operators often keep a single ordered model catalog in `agents.defaults.models`, so the duplication requirement was easy to miss.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: derive failover candidates from `agents.defaults.models` only when `fallbacksFromModels: true`, keep explicit `fallbacks` precedence, and keep `fallbacks: []` as an intentional disable.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the behavior is isolated to fallback candidate construction before provider execution.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing `runWithModelFallback` unit coverage already covers explicit fallback ordering and allowlist behavior.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New opt-in config: `agents.defaults.model.fallbacksFromModels: true`
- When enabled and explicit `fallbacks` are omitted, OpenClaw derives fallback candidates from `agents.defaults.models` in config order, excluding the configured primary.
- Explicit `fallbacks` still win, and `fallbacks: []` still disables fallback.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[primary model fails] -> [check explicit fallbacks only] -> [stop if none configured]

After:
[primary model fails] -> [explicit fallbacks?]
                    -> [if none + fallbacksFromModels=true, derive from models catalog]
                    -> [try next configured model]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (No)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (No)
- New/changed network calls? (No)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (No)
- Data access scope changed? (No)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:

## Repro + Verification

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two `response.json()` calls in feishu streaming-card.ts read Feishu API responses without a read limit. An oversized response from the Feishu token or create-card endpoints could buffer arbitrarily large payloads before parsing, risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

All external HTTP response reads should use `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). The file already uses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` for SSRF protection — this adds memory bounding.

## Evidence

### Committed test proof

The test suite includes a dedicated oversized response rejection test that creates an 18 MiB `ReadableStream` body, passes it through the Feishu streaming card session flow, and verifies both the error message and stream cancellation:

```ts
it("rejects oversized token responses and cancels the stream", async () => {
  let canceled = false;
  const ONE_MIB = 1024 * 1024;
  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    start(controller) {
      for (let i = 0; i < 18; i++) controller.enqueue(new Uint8Array(ONE_MIB));
      controller.close();
    },
    cancel() { canceled = true; },
  });
  // ... feeds oversized body through FeishuStreamingSession ...
  expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
  expect((error as Error).message).toContain("feishu.streamingCard.token");
  expect(canceled).toBe(true);
});
```

### Local test run — 19/19 passed

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > flushes throttled pending text after the throttle window 25ms
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > pushes natural-boundary updates immediately inside the throttle window
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > retries cumulative content after a failed streaming update
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > retries cumulative content after a non-OK streaming update
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > replaces content when final text removes transient streamed status
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > drops a surrogate pair whole when truncating the closeout summary
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > logs a final replacement failure when CardKit returns non-OK
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > reports no visible content when final close update fails before any accepted text
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token cache lifetime when token expiry overflows
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token fallback lifetime when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > treats an invalid process clock as a streaming token cache miss
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > prefers the latest full text when it already includes prior text
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > keeps previous text when the next partial is empty or redundant
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > appends fragmented chunks without injecting newlines
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > merges overlap between adjacent partial snapshots
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > prefers message.reply when reply target and root id both exist
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > falls back to root create when reply target is absent
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > uses create mode when no reply routing fields are provided
 ✓ Feishu streaming card oversized response rejection > rejects oversized token responses and cancels the stream 44ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### What changed

- `streaming-card.ts`: replaced `response.json()` calls with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap)
- `streaming-card.test.ts`: updated mock responses to use real `Response` objects; added oversized rejection test

## Risk

Low. 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses. Same `readProviderJsonResponse` helper used across all provider JSON reads.

## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2-5 bullets:

- Problem: when tools are explicitly disabled for a session, OpenClaw can still build a prompt that looks partly like a normal tool-enabled session. That can leave behind leaked skills content or other tool-only guidance.
- Why it matters: if the prompt says the session has tools when it actually does not, the model can try to use tools that are unavailable and behave like a tool-enabled session instead of a chat-only one.
- What changed: this PR makes the no-tools case consistent in the code that builds and adjusts the system prompt. The final prompt, prompt report, CLI path, embedded-runner path, and OpenAI-specific no-tools wording now all agree when a session really has no tools. It also fixes skills reporting in cases where the prompt contains another <available_skills> block or a skill body contains headings like # Project Context. Before this change, the prompt report could read the wrong block or stop too early, which could make it show missing or partial skills even though the real prompt still contained them.
- Additional behavior corrected: sessions that only have hosted/client tools no longer advertise OpenClaw built-in tool flows such as exec or subagents when those built-in tools are not actually available.
- Small contract update: provider-specific prompt code now receives `toolNames` in the `transformSystemPrompt` context, so plugins see the same advertised tool list that the main prompt builder is using.
- Scope boundary: this PR does not broadly redesign all capability handling. Sessions with omitted tool lists or non-empty filtered tool lists are still left mostly unchanged unless a narrow fix was needed to keep the no-tools and hosted-tool-only cases truthful.

- Root cause: when OpenClaw builds the system prompt for a session with no tools, different parts of the prompt-building flow can disagree about whether tools are available. Some parts correctly treat the session as tool-free, while others still act as if tools or skills exist, so the final prompt can end up mixing no-tool behavior with tool-related guidance.

target.title: feat(doctor): add Node.js runtime info health contribution
target.body:
## Summary
Add a new Doctor health contribution that displays Node.js runtime
diagnostics during `openclaw doctor`, providing essential context for
troubleshooting and proactive upgrade guidance.
## What it does
**Runtime summary note** (always shown):
Node 24.14.0 · ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node · via nvm
**Version manager detection** — identifies nvm, fnm, volta, asdf, n,
nodenv, nodebrew, and nvs from the executable path.
**Proactive warnings** (when applicable):
- Node version below minimum (>=22.19.0) — rarely triggers since the
  startup gate catches this first, but guards edge cases
- Node release in maintenance phase — shows months remaining until EOL
- Node release past end-of-life — recommends a current Active LTS release
- Older-than-recommended LTS — gentle nudge toward the recommended LTS
## Why
Doctor currently has no visibility into the Node.js runtime environment.
When users share Doctor output in issues or with maintainers, the Node
version and installation method are critical diagnostic context that was
previously missing.
This reuses existing infrastructure:
- `runtime-guard.ts` — `detectRuntime()`, `parseSemver()`, `runtimeSatisfies()`
- `runtime-paths.ts` — `isVersionManagedNodePath()`
No new dependencies. No runtime behavior changes outside of Doctor.
## Changes
New files:
- `src/commands/doctor-node-runtime.ts` (~200 lines) — diagnostics
  collection, warning generation, summary formatting, contribution entry
- `src/commands/doctor-node-runtime.test.ts` — 27 unit tests
Modified:
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — +1 import, +1 wrapper
  function, +1 contribution registration (after `bundled-plugin-runtime-deps`,
  before `state-integrity`)
## Test plan
- `pnpm check` — 0 errors ✅
- `vitest` — 27/27 tests ✅
- `pnpm build` — clean ✅
Test coverage:
- `detectVersionManagerName`: 11 tests (null, system, nvm, fnm, volta,
  asdf, n, nodenv, nodebrew, nvs, Windows backslash)
- `collectNodeRuntimeDiagnostics`: 3 tests (nvm path, unknown runtime,
  system install)
- `buildNodeRuntimeWarnings`: 8 tests (recommended version, below
  minimum, past EOL, maintenance phase, pre-maintenance nudge, current
  recommended, null major, future major)
- `buildNodeRuntimeSummary`: 5 tests (system install, named manager,
  unknown manager, null version, separator format)
---
## Real behavior proof
_Refreshed for current head `f90eee0a` (after the Windows case-insensitive OS-home redaction commit)._

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Doctor Node runtime note renders the executable path via a two-pass redaction (`shortenHomePath` for the OpenClaw home, then an OS-home pass). The OS-home pass compared the Windows home prefix with exact casing, so a valid Windows path whose drive/username casing differed from `os.homedir()` (e.g. `os.homedir()` = `C:\Users\Alice`, `execPath` = `c:\users\alice\...`) fell through unredacted and leaked the OS username. POSIX comparison stays case-sensitive; the Windows backslash-boundary prefix is now compared case-insensitively, slicing by the original length to preserve real casing.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, WSL2), Node.js 24.14.0, current PR head `f90eee0a`. Invoked the real `collectNodeRuntimeDiagnostics()` + `buildNodeRuntimeSummary()` — the same render `noteNodeRuntime()` emits in the Doctor health flow — plus injected lifecycle scenarios via the exported helpers.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ran the registered render path via tsx against the real runtime:
```bash
$ node --import tsx run-node-runtime-note.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix (current head):** Block 1 is the real render on this machine. Block 2 is the POSIX OS-home redaction scenario (OPENCLAW_HOME elsewhere). Block 3 is the new Windows case-insensitive redaction this commit fixes. Remaining blocks are injected lifecycle scenarios against the current date.
```
=== 1. Real current-head render (Node v24.14.0) ===
Node 24.14.0 · /usr/bin/node · system install

=== 2. POSIX OS-home redaction (OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw, Node under the user's OS home) ===
os home (HOME)     : /home/<user>
input  execPath    : /home/<user>/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node
output rendered    : Node 24.14.0 · ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node · via nvm
leaks OS username? : NO (redacted)

=== 3. Windows case-insensitive redaction (the new fix) ===
os.homedir()       : C:\Users\Alice   (canonical casing)
input  execPath    : c:\users\alice\AppData\Roaming\nvm\v24.14.0\node.exe   (lower-cased)
output rendered    : Node 24.14.0 · ~\AppData\Roaming\nvm\v24.14.0\node.exe · via nvm
leaks OS username? : NO (redacted)

=== Injected Node 22 LTS (22.19.0, in maintenance) ===
Node 22 LTS is in maintenance mode (EOL 2027-04-30, ~10 months remaining).
Consider upgrading to Node 24 for the latest features and longer support.

=== Injected Node 20 (20.18.0, below the >=22.19.0 minimum) ===
Node 20.18.0 does not meet the minimum requirement (>=22.19.0).
Upgrade Node: https://nodejs.org/en/download
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The real Node 24.14.0 runtime renders a clean note (supported, system install). Both the POSIX OS-home scenario (block 2) and the Windows case-mismatch scenario (block 3) now redact the home to `~`, so no OS username appears — including when `execPath` casing differs from `os.homedir()`. Before this commit, the exact-case Windows prefix check left such paths unredacted. Injected Node 22 LTS / 20 produce the expected maintenance / below-minimum advisories. POSIX, Windows OPENCLAW_HOME-override, and the new Windows case-mismatch regression tests cover the redaction paths; 51 unit tests pass, types and lint clean.

- **What was not tested:** The full interactive `openclaw doctor` TUI run was not captured (it triggers a heavy dist build); the registered render path is invoked directly instead. Redaction relies on `os.homedir()`; in the rare case where `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` is unset and differs from the path's owner (e.g. some sudo/container setups), redaction may not apply — out of scope for this detect-only diagnostic.

target.body: # Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: The macOS chat bubble color is hardcoded to a static blue, with no way for users to personalize it. - Why it matters: Users want visual customization of the chat interface to match their preferences or distinguish between instances. - What changed: Added a new "Colors" settings tab with a 10-color palette picker, a custom `ColorPicker`, and a system accent color toggle. `ColorPreferencesStore` (in `OpenClawKit`) persists preferences via `UserDefaults` and exposes a `resolvedColor` that `ChatTheme.userBubble` now reads on macOS. `userText` dynamically picks black or white based on WCAG relative luminance. A cross-platform `ColorHexSupport` utility was added to `OpenClawKit` for hex-to-Color and Color-to-hex conversions. The macOS-local `ColorHexSupport` gained a reverse `hex(from:)` helper. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): iOS chat bubble color remains the existing static blue. ## Change Type (select all) - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes # - Related # - [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable) N/A ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) N/A ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - macOS: New "Colors" tab in Settings (between "Channels" and "Skills") with three selection modes: system accent color (default, preserves existing behavior), palette color (10 curated colors from Apple's Human Interface Guidelines), or arbitrary custom color via `ColorPicker`. - Chat bubble color updates live when a new color is selected; preferences persist across app restarts via `UserDefaults`. - User message text automatically switches between white and black depending on the chosen bubble color's luminance (WCAG threshold at 0.6). ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text Before: [user message] -> [hardcoded rgb(127,184,212) bubble] -> [white text] After: [user message] -> [ColorPreferencesStore.resolvedColor] -> [palette / custom / accent bubble] -> [WCAG luminance > 0.6?] -> yes -> [black text] -> no -> [white text] ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS 15+ - Runtime/container: Swift 6 / SwiftUI - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): N/A - Relevant config (redacted): N/A ### Steps 1. Build and launch the macOS app. 2. Open Settings > Colors. 3. Select a palette color, apply a custom color, or toggle "Use Accent Color." 4. Open a chat session see the selected color on your messages. ### Expected - User chat bubble reflects the selected color. - Text is white on dark bubbles and black on light bubbles (e.g. yellow). - Preference survives app restart. ### Actual - Verified as expected. ## Evidence Attach at least one: - [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) **Color palette** **Custom color** **Dark text on bright color** ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: Palette selection, custom color via ColorPicker, accent color toggle, preference persistence across restart, live bubble color update in chat. - Edge cases checked: Light colors (yellow, orange) produce black text; dark colors (indigo, blue) produce white text. Clearing custom color falls back to palette or accent. Off-main-thread `resolvedColor` defaults to light palette variant. - What you did **not** verify: iOS runtime (feature is macOS-only for now). No automated Swift tests were added for the new views or store. ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: `ColorPreferencesStore.shared` is `nonisolated(unsafe)` and initialized eagerly in `AppState.init`; concurrent first access from a background thread could race. - Mitigation: `AppState` calls `_ = ColorPreferencesStore.shared` during init on the main actor, ensuring the singleton is created before any background reader. - Risk: `UserDefaults`-backed preferences do not sync across macOS reinstalls or profiles. - Mitigation: Defaults to system accent color (existing behavior); preferences are non-critical and easily re-set.

target.title: fix(acpx): validate parsed PIDs with Number.isFinite in parseProcessList
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `parseProcessList` applies `Number.parseInt` to PID/PPID values from `ps` output without validating the parsed result. NaN values could propagate to `process.kill()`, which throws on non-finite arguments.

**Solution**: Add a `Number.isFinite` guard after `Number.parseInt` to reject non-finite values at parse time, matching the pattern from PR #98371.

**What changed**: `extensions/acpx/src/process-reaper.ts` — assign parsed pid/ppid to locals, skip non-finite values with `continue`, push valid entries unchanged.

**What did NOT change**: No behavior change on valid input. The regex still requires digit-only pid/ppid groups. All 146 existing ACPX tests pass identically.

## What Problem This Solves

`parseProcessList` applies `Number.parseInt` to PID and PPID values extracted from `ps` output without validating the parsed result. While the current regex (`\d+`) captures only digits, a future regex change could produce `NaN` values that propagate to `process.kill()`, which throws on non-finite PID arguments.

This is the same class of issue that PR #98371 fixed in `src/cli/ports.ts`. The same `isValidPid()` pattern exists in `src/shared/pid-alive.ts`, but as per the extension boundary rules, this fix uses `Number.isFinite` directly inline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Defensive programming: catch malformed PID/PPID values at parse time rather than relying on downstream guards (`uniquePids` filters `Number.isInteger(pid) && pid > 0`, but NaN might bypass that check in unexpected code paths). Consistent with the pattern applied in PR #98371.

## User Impact

None on correct `ps` output. The regex still requires digit-only pid/ppid groups, so all valid process entries pass through unchanged. Invalid (non-finite) entries are silently skipped, matching the existing behavior of skipping non-matching lines.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Defensive Number.isFinite guard after Number.parseInt in parseProcessList to prevent NaN PID/PPID from reaching process.kill()

- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.1.0, ext4 filesystem, local machine. Evidence script uses the exact regex and logic from process-reaper.ts with real `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,command=` stdout.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # Evidence script (replicates parseProcessList with exact regex + both before/after logic):
  node /home/.../evidence/pr-99010/evidence-collection.ts
  
  # Unit tests:
  pnpm test extensions/acpx
  ```

- **After-fix evidence**:
  ```

target.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #58822.

- Restores correct subagent model precedence in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`: global `agents.defaults.subagents.model` now takes priority over the parent agent's own `model.primary`, with the agent's own model only used as a last-resort fallback
- Applies the same fix to the cron isolated-agent model selection path (`src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`) and the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper in `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Updates existing tests from #58003 to assert the corrected behavior and adds new coverage for main-agent, named-agent, and explicit-override scenarios

### Background

PR #58003 reordered `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection` to prefer `agentConfig.model` over `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. While this was intended to let named agents keep their own model for subagents, it caused a regression: when the main agent runs Opus and `defaults.subagents.model` is GPT-5.4, subagents incorrectly inherited Opus because the agent's own model shadowed the global subagent default.

The correct precedence is:
1. `agentConfig.subagents.model` — explicit per-agent subagent config (highest)
2. `agents.defaults.subagents.model` — global subagent default
3. `agentConfig.model` — agent's own model (last-resort fallback)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 105 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` — 32 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` — 11 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-spawn.model-session.test.ts` — 1 test passes
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` — 84 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — 34 tests pass
- [x] Test: main agent (Opus) with global subagent default (GPT-5.4) → subagents use GPT-5.4
- [x] Test: named agent without per-agent subagents.model → uses global default
- [x] Test: falls back to agent own model when no global default set
- [x] Test: explicit model override in spawn always wins

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Subagent model resolution for a main agent whose own `model` differs from `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. Before this PR, an Opus-running agent with `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5` still produced Opus subagents because the agent's own `model` shadowed the global subagent default in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, in the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, and in the cron isolated-agent path. This PR restores the documented precedence so the global default wins over the agent's primary model, while per-agent `subagents.model` still takes the very top slot.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64 (Node v24.15.0), local checkout of `fix/subagent-model-precedence-global-default` at HEAD `81168e5de5`, dependencies installed via `pnpm install`. Resolvers exercised by importing the actual TypeScript source under `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/agents/agent-scope.ts` via the `tsx` loader — no mocks, no Vitest, no provider catalogs swapped out. The cron isolated-agent path uses the same `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, so the asserted source values cover that resolver too.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ cd pr-58823
$ pnpm install --prefer-offline
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs
```

The script (`scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs`, committed in this PR for reviewer reproducibility) constructs three real `OpenClawConfig` shapes, calls `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult`, `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, and `resolveSubagentSpawnModelSelection` on each, and asserts both the resolved model ref and the selection `source` label (`subagent` / `default-subagent` / `agent`).

**Evidence after fix:** Verbatim terminal stdout (runtime log) from the live `node --import tsx` run above against the patched sources:

```
PR #58823 subagent model precedence — real-behavior proof
repo head: (local worktree)
node: v24.15.0

--- scenario A — global default beats agent primary ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = default-subagent
agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5
OK scenario A — global default beats agent primary

--- scenario B — per-agent override wins ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = openai/gpt-5-mini
agent-scope source                   = subagent
agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5-mini"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5-mini
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5-mini
OK scenario B — per-agent override wins

--- scenario C — falls through to agent primary ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = (unset)
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = agent
agent-scope raw                      = "anthropic/claude-opus"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = anthropic/claude-opus
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = anthropic/claude-opus
OK scenario C — falls through to agent primary

PROOF PASSED — subagent model precedence follows: per-agent > defaults.subagents > agent primary
```

For completeness, the Vitest suites listed in Test plan also pass on this branch (`pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` → 105 passed; `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` → 32 passed; etc.), but the authoritative proof above is the live `node --import tsx` run against the actual patched source files, not the unit suite.

**Observed result after fix:**

- Scenario A (Opus main agent, `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5`, no per-agent override): the live resolver returns `openai/gpt-5` with `source = default-subagent`. Before this PR it returned `anthropic/claude-opus` with `source = agent` — the exact bug from #58822.
- Scenario B (per-agent `subagents.model = openai/gpt-5-mini` set alongside the global default): `openai/gpt-5-mini` with `source = subagent` wins. Per-agent override still beats the global default, confirming the highest-priority rung is intact.
- Scenario C (neither per-agent `subagents.model` nor `defaults.subagents.model` set): resolves to the agent's own `model` (`anthropic/claude-opus`) with `source = agent`, confirming the documented last-resort fallback is preserved.

The `node` exit code was `0` (proof script asserts each expectation; first mismatch would throw). The `agent-scope` source labels are produced by the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper used by both `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`, so a passing scope source label means the cron path inherits the same precedence.

**What was not tested:** Cross-OS runtime (macOS / Windows) — code path is platform-agnostic config resolution, no filesystem or shell dependencies. Live spawn of an actual subagent process against a remote model provider — the resolver returns the same model ref regardless of whether the downstream spawn succeeds, and the spawn path is exercised by `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` (11 passing). UI surfacing of the resolved subagent model in the gateway is also unchanged by this PR and not re-tested here.

target.title: fix(memory-host): add AbortSignal support to batch polling (OpenAI, Voyage, Gemini)
target.body:
Add AbortSignal support to batch polling loops to enable immediate cancellation when clients disconnect.

Problem
When HTTP clients disconnect during batch embedding operations, server-side polling continues until timeout, wasting API quota.

Solution
- Replace uncancelable setTimeout with cancellable version using clearTimeout
- Add signal?: AbortSignal parameter to all batch providers
- Use { once: true } to prevent listener accumulation (fixes MaxListenersExceededWarning)
- Thread signal through full call chain: batch-runner → runXxxBatches → waitForXxxBatch

Changes
- batch-runner.ts: Add signal to EmbeddingBatchExecutionParams type
- batch-openai.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup
- batch-voyage.ts: Update sleep type, add signal threading through deps
- batch-gemini.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup

Testing
- Verified polling stops within 1s of abort (was 30+ iterations)
- No listener leaks after long polls
- TypeScript compiles without errors

Backwards Compatible: signal is optional.

**Additional Fixes (Post-Review)**:
- Fixed `initial: batchInfo` parameter regression in `batch-voyage.ts` and `batch-gemini.ts` to avoid extra API calls on batch creation
- Fixed locale regression in `ui/src/ui/presenter.ts` (reverted hardcoded "en-US" to `undefined` for i18n compliance)

target.title: feat(plugins): add optional api.resetSession()
target.body:
## Summary

`main` already has gateway-side session reset support through `performGatewaySessionReset()`.

This PR adds optional plugin-side `api.resetSession(key, reason?)` support on top of the current mainline architecture.

- Adds `PluginResetSessionResult` type and optional `resetSession` on `OpenClawPluginApi`
- Wires `api.resetSession(...)` in the plugin registry only in full registration mode and only when the gateway exposes `sessions.reset`
- Reuses gateway-owned canonicalization and reset resolution (no plugin-side duplicate logic)
- Unifies config snapshot usage in `performGatewaySessionReset` to eliminate config-drift between target resolution and entry lookup
- Adds per-canonical-key in-flight guard in the reset service
- Exports `PluginResetSessionResult` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/core`

## Scope

This PR:
- adds `PluginResetSessionResult` to `src/plugins/types.ts`
- adds optional `resetSession` to `OpenClawPluginApi`
- adds builder support in `src/plugins/api-builder.ts`
- wires `api.resetSession(...)` in `src/plugins/registry.ts` (full-mode + capability gated)
- adds optional `existingCfg` param to `loadSessionEntry` in `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`
- adds in-flight guard and unified resolution in `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts`
- exports the result type from `src/plugin-sdk/core.ts`
- adds focused plugin contract tests (17 tests)
- refreshes generated plugin SDK API baselines

This PR does not:
- change gateway reset RPC behavior
- broaden session architecture scope beyond the plugin API surface
- revive any stale-branch refactor baggage from the closed #43375

## Behavior

`api.resetSession(key, reason?)`:
- accepts `"new"` or `"reset"` reason values (defaults to `"new"`)
- trims and validates the key
- delegates to gateway-owned `performGatewaySessionReset`
- resolves to a structured plugin result instead of rejecting for operational failures
- absent in setup-only, setup-runtime, and cli-metadata registration modes
- absent when gateway does not expose `sessions.reset`

Success: `{ ok: true, key, sessionId }`
Failure: `{ ok: false, key, code, message }`

target.title: fix(find): prevent recursive re-entry in child kill via sentinel guard (#98961)
target.body:
Fixes #98961.

## What Problem This Solves

In `find.ts`, `child.on("error")` only called `cleanup()` (which closed readline), while `child.on("close")` called both `cleanup()` and `stopChild?.()`. On spawn failure or certain error paths, the child process was not killed — leaving a potential orphan.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes with a safety sentinel:

1. **`cleanup()` now calls `stopChild?.()`** — so both error and close handlers stop the child symmetrically.

2. **`stopChild` uses a `stopChildKilling` sentinel** — prevents recursive re-entry if `child.kill()` triggers Node's `error` event before `settle` clears the hook.

This avoids the risk ClawSweeper identified in PR #98854: a direct `stopChild?.()` in the error handler can recursively re-enter the kill path.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Asymmetric child cleanup in fd find tool's error handler.

**Real environment tested**: Node 22.19+, local OpenClaw checkout.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx -e "..."
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
=== PROOF: fd find-tool sentinel error/stop ===

  [error event] spawn __nonexistent_fd_binary__ ENOENT
  [error handler] calling cleanup()...
  cleanup: rl.close() + stopChild?.()
  stopChild: → kill() child
  [close event] code=-2
  [close handler] calling cleanup()...
  cleanup: rl.close() + stopChild?.()
  stopChild: SKIPPED (sentinel/killed)
  ✅ sentinel prevented recursive kill

error event: true
close event: true
stopChild called: true
child killed: false

✅ PROOF PASSED
```

The sentinel blocks the redundant second kill when `close` re-enters after `error`. No loop, no crash.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts
 (passed, exit 0)
```

**Observed result after fix**: A non-existent tool spawn triggers `error` → `cleanup()` → `stopChild?.()` → kill safely. Sentinel guards against recursive re-entry.

**What was not tested**: E2E with a real `fd` binary across all edge cases. The proof covers the spawn-failure path — the primary error scenario for this helper.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.test.ts --run` — 2 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts` — exit 0

## Root Cause

`child.on("error")` at original line 297 called `cleanup()` (rl.close) but skipped `stopChild?.()`. The close handler called both. The direct 1-line fix proposed in #98854 carries a risk of recursive kill if `child.kill()` emits another `error` before `settle` clears the hook. The sentinel-guarded approach avoids this.

target.title: fix: before_agent_run transform no longer leaks redacted text into history
target.body:
Closes #96656 (reopens with the redesigned fix)

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins can register a `before_agent_run` hook that returns `{ outcome: "transform", prompt }` to redact or rewrite a user's prompt before it reaches the model — for example, masking a credit card number. Previously this only replaced the prompt sent to the model for that single turn; the original, unredacted text was still persisted into session history. On any later turn, the model could read the raw sensitive text back out of history, defeating the purpose of the redaction.

This affected both execution backends: the embedded agent runner (used by most model providers) and the CLI-native harness runner (used by Codex/Copilot-style CLI backends).

## Why This Change Was Made

A `transform` decision now writes the same redacted text to both the model input and the persisted session transcript, so a redaction stays redacted for the rest of the conversation instead of leaking back in on a later turn.

- Embedded runner: the transformed prompt is now used as the transcript-bound text too, so `session.prompt(...)` persists the redacted version. The existing model/transcript prompt-swap mechanism (used for an unrelated "extra context for the model" feature) becomes a no-op in this case since both sides already match.
- CLI-native harness runner: its user-turn transcript recorder captures the raw message *before* the hook runs, so there was no existing seam to inject a replacement. Added an `overrideMessage` option to the recorder's `persistApproved()` so a transform decision can swap in the redacted text while preserving the message's other metadata (media, timestamp, idempotency key).

Non-goal: this does not redact prompts from historical turns that were already persisted before this fix, or from other logging/observability surfaces outside the session transcript.

## User Impact

Plugin authors building guardrail/redaction plugins (e.g., PII masking, secret scrubbing) can now trust that a `transform` decision fully removes the original text from the conversation going forward, not just from the current model call.

## Evidence

Reviewers can run these tests directly; both encode the exact scenario (redacting a credit card number) and assert on the actually-persisted content:

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts
```

`attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts` → `uses before_agent_run transform at both the model boundary and the session transcript` asserts the transcript-bound prompt captured via `sessionPrompt` equals the redacted text, not the original.

`cli-runner.reliability.test.ts` → `uses before_agent_run transform for CLI model input and the persisted transcript` reads the actual session JSONL file written to disk and asserts the last line contains the redacted text and does not contain the raw card number.

Reverting either fix commit (`aec760012e` / `1bf4a9655f`) makes its corresponding test fail — the tests previously asserted the *old* (leaking) behavior and were updated as part of this change.

### Manual reproduction

Anyone can reproduce the leak-then-fix behavior locally with a minimal plugin. Save as `~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-pii-redact/index.js` (plus a sibling `package.json` with `"openclaw": { "extensions": ["./index.js"] }` and an `openclaw.plugin.json` with `id`, `name`, and an empty `configSchema`):

```js
const CREDIT_CARD_RE = /\b(?:\d{4}[-\s]?){3}\d{4}\b/g;

export default {
  id: "demo-pii-redact",
  register(api) {
    api.on("before_agent_run", async (event) => {
      const redacted = event.prompt.replace(CREDIT_CARD_RE, "[CreditCardNumber]");
      if (redacted === event.prompt) return { outcome: "pass" };
      return { outcome: "transform", prompt: redacted, reason: "PII redaction" };
    });
  },
};
```

Then:

```bash
openclaw plugins enable demo-pii-redact
openclaw config set plugins.entries.demo-pii-redact.hooks.allowConversationAccess true --strict-json
openclaw chat
```

Send `My credit card is 4111-1111-1111-1111`, then ask `What card number did I just give you?` in the same session. Before this fix, the model can still recall the raw number from history; after this fix, only `[CreditCardNumber]` is ever visible to the model, on this turn and every later one.

target.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #51620 — gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages.

## Changes

### New: `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.ts`
Serializes all non-empty `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` entries to `state/pending-messages.json` before shutdown. Strips non-portable fields (`config`, `skillsSnapshot`) and stores a version marker + timestamp.

### New: `src/gateway/server-pending-messages.ts`
On startup, reads the persisted file, injects missed messages as system events into their respective sessions (so the agent processes them on next turn), then deletes the file. Includes a 5-minute staleness guard to avoid replaying ancient messages from stale files.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-close.ts`
Calls `persistFollowupQueues(FOLLOWUP_QUEUES)` before `chatRunState.clear()` so queue state is captured while still available. Best-effort — failure doesn't block shutdown.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-startup.ts`
Calls `replayPersistedPendingMessages()` 1.5s after startup (after channels initialize), alongside the existing `scheduleRestartSentinelWake`.

## Tests

16 new tests covering:
- `persistFollowupQueues`: empty queues, non-empty queues, config stripping, multiple queues
- `consumePersistedQueues`: no file, read+delete, staleness guard (>5min), corrupt file, wrong version
- Round-trip: persist → consume
- `replayPersistedPendingMessages`: no entries, empty entries, system event injection, multiple queues, prompt truncation, empty items skip

## Limitations / Follow-up

This PR covers **Phase 1**: persisting in-memory followup queue items across restart.

Still not covered (follow-up work):
- **Phase 2**: Messages arriving during the drain window (hitting `GatewayDrainingError`) — these are rejected at the channel level before reaching the queue
- **Phase 3**: Channel-level message acknowledgment deferral — for channels that support it (Slack Socket Mode), defer ACK until message is processed or persisted so the platform can redeliver

## Testing

```
npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.test.ts src/gateway/server-pending-messages.test.ts
```

All 16 tests pass.

Adds complete bidirectional Signal quote-reply support — both outbound (agent → user) and inbound (user → agent) quote context handling.

## Problem

**Outbound (agent → user):** When the assistant includes reply tags (`[[reply_to_current]]`, `[[reply_to:<id>]]`), they were stripped but never translated into signal-cli quote parameters. Signal showed no visual reply indicator, unlike Discord/Telegram/Slack.

**Inbound (user → agent):** When a user quote-replies to the agent, the quoted message context was either lost or only used as fallback body text. The agent had no structured awareness of what was being quoted, who wrote it, or that a quote-reply was even happening.

## Solution

### Outbound Changes (agent → user)

1. **Signal outbound adapter** (`src/channels/plugins/outbound/signal.ts`)
   - Updated `sendText()` and `sendMedia()` to pass `replyToId` and `quoteAuthor`

2. **Signal send function** (`src/signal/send.ts`)
   - Added `replyTo` and `quoteAuthor` to `SignalSendOpts`
   - Converts `replyTo` timestamp into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params
   - Uses `Number()` instead of `parseInt()` for strict timestamp validation
   - Guards group quotes: skips quoting when `quoteAuthor` is missing (avoids silent signal-cli failures)

3. **Delivery layer** (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`)
   - `trackReplyConsumption` pattern for bestEffort partial-failure handling
   - `sendPayload` branch routes through quote gating
   - Reply metadata consumed only after successful send
   - Per-payload explicit `replyToId` preserved independently of inherited reply

4. **Event handler — outbound** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - `resolveQuotedAuthor()` with LRU cache for group quote-author resolution
   - Only falls back to current sender for `[[reply_to_current]]`, not explicit `[[reply_to:<id>]]`

### Inbound Changes (user → agent)

5. **Expanded quote types** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.types.ts`)
   - `SignalQuote` type captures full signal-cli payload: `id`, `author`, `authorNumber`, `authorUuid`, `text`, `mentions`, `attachments`, `textStyles`
   - New `SignalQuotedAttachment`, `SignalTextStyle`, `SignalReplyTarget` types

6. **Quote context module** (`src/signal/monitor/quote-context.ts` — NEW)
   - `describeSignalReplyTarget()` extracts structured quote context from inbound messages
   - `normalizeSignalQuoteId()` validates quote timestamps with strict `Number()` parsing
   - Author resolution cascade: `authorNumber` → `authorUuid` → `author` → LRU cache fallback
   - Handles mentions in quoted text, media attachment placeholders, edge cases

7. **Structured context surfacing** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - Inbound quotes surfaced as `ReplyToId`, `ReplyToBody`, `ReplyToSender`, `ReplyToIsQuote`
   - Both the user message AND the quoted text are preserved
   - Group and DM quote handling unified

### Tests

- Comprehensive test suite for outbound quote mechanics
- New `event-handler.inbound-contract.test.ts` for inbound quote contract tests
- Refactored `event-handler.quote.test.ts` with edge case coverage
- All tests passing

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Outbound Signal quote-reply parameters were never translated into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params, and inbound user quote-replies were dropped or only surfaced as fallback body text. target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

  sess=agent:main:subagent:task42         → 2 files

target.title: fix: avoid English audio prompt for non-English STT hints
target.body:
Closes #98970.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users transcribing short non-English audio with an explicit audio language hint, such as `language=ru`, could still receive an English translation when no custom audio prompt was configured. The affected workflow is provider-backed audio transcription through OpenAI-compatible STT providers such as Groq Whisper.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw previously resolved the built-in English audio prompt, `Transcribe the audio.`, before building provider transcription requests, so the provider could receive both a non-English language hint and an English prompt. This change keeps explicit prompts and English/default-language behavior intact, but omits only OpenClaw's implicit English audio prompt when the provider audio request has a non-English language hint.

The fix stays in shared media-understanding provider request construction instead of adding a Groq-only branch. The OpenAI-compatible adapter already omits undefined multipart fields, so when the runner leaves `prompt` unset the outgoing form keeps `language=ru` and has no `prompt` field.

## User Impact

Non-English voice notes are less likely to be silently translated into English when users already configured the audio language hint for transcription. Users who set an explicit audio prompt still get that exact prompt, and English or no-language transcription keeps the existing default prompt behavior.

## Evidence

Groq contract checked from current docs:

- [Groq Speech to Text](https://console.groq.com/docs/speech-to-text) separates `/audio/transcriptions` from `/audio/translations`; translations are the endpoint that translates audio to English.
- [Groq API reference](https://console.groq.com/docs/api-reference) documents transcription `language` as an optional ISO-639-1 input language hint and `prompt` as optional text that should match the audio language.

target.title: fix(gateway): tighten CSP connect-src from bare ws:/wss: to explicit endpoints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI CSP `connect-src` directive used bare scheme sources `ws:` and `wss:`. Per CSP spec, a bare scheme source allows connections to **any** host — meaning any XSS in the Control UI could exfiltrate data via WebSocket to an arbitrary server.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI actually only needs three specific WebSocket/connection targets beyond `'self'`:
1. **Gateway WebSocket** — same origin, covered by `'self'`
2. **OpenAI API** — `https://api.openai.com` (already explicitly listed, HTTPS)
3. **Google Gemini Live** — `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` for realtime voice feature (was relying on bare `wss:`)

Rather than allowing "any WebSocket anywhere", the policy now explicitly names each endpoint.

## User Impact

- **No visible change** — all existing functionality works identically
- Defense-in-depth improvement if a future XSS vulnerability is discovered in the Control UI

## Evidence

- ~60 CSP unit tests pass (4 test files, all green)~
- Verified that:
  - `gateway.ts:520` — Gateway WebSocket uses page origin (`'self'`)
  - `realtime-talk-google-live.ts:106` — Google Live WebSocket uses `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (now explicitly listed)
  - `realtime-talk-webrtc.ts:126` — OpenAI Realtime uses HTTPS `fetch` to `api.openai.com` (already listed)

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Real test run on commit 6bc5dce5 (latest, after switching to strict PID parsing and restoring the dedupe test):

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Start at  09:10:41
   Duration  2.02s (transform 1.88s, setup 1.15s, import 108ms, tests 529ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.71s
```

16 tests (up from 14): the previously-replaced "deduplicates repeated lsof listener records" test is restored, plus a new regression test for truncated pid tokens (`p111abc`).

### Real Behavior Proof (addresses prior "mock-only" finding)

Codex's prior review correctly flagged that the evidence only showed Vitest mock output and stale code (`Number.parseInt`). Below is the actual production parsing function executed directly with `tsx`, no test framework, no mocks — comparing the old truncating behavior against the new strict behavior on the exact malformed token Codex called out.

```bash
$ tsx /tmp/pid-proof.mjs
=== Real production code execution (no mocks) ===
Legacy behavior:  Number.parseInt("111abc", 10) = 111
Fixed behavior:   parseStrictPositiveInteger("111abc") = undefined

Legacy behavior would have accepted pid 111 from a corrupted lsof "p" record.
Fixed behavior correctly returns undefined so the record is dropped.
```

`parseStrictPositiveInteger` is imported directly from `packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts` (the same helper already used elsewhere in `ports-inspect.ts`), so this is the real shipped implementation, not a re-implementation for the proof.

**Current fix** at `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:53-56`:
```typescript
if (line.startsWith("p")) {
  const pid = parseStrictPositiveInteger(line.slice(1));
  processFields = pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {};
}
```

**End-to-end proof via the malformed-token regression test** (`src/infra/ports.test.ts`, "rejects lsof pid tokens with trailing garbage instead of truncating them"): feeding `lsof` output `p111abc\ncnode\nnTCP *:18789 (LISTEN)\n` through `inspectPortUsage()` now yields `result.listeners.length === 0` — the record is dropped instead of being mis-attributed to pid 111. Verified in the same real Vitest run above.

**Test Coverage:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Empty/missing pid record (`p` with no digits) → skipped
- Truncated/garbage-suffixed pid token (`p111abc`) → skipped (regression for the parseInt truncation bug)
- Repeated identical listener records for one process/address → deduplicated

target.body:
## Summary

- Add bounded retry handling for transient `FsSafeError: path-mismatch` while writing imported memory-wiki source pages.
- Coalesce concurrent bridge imported-source syncs for the same resolved vault/config so `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace` share the same in-flight bridge sync instead of launching duplicate import/index-refresh passes.
- Preserve existing vault safety boundaries for symlink/path-alias and directory-collision cases.
- Rebase the existing PR onto current `origin/main` and keep main's shared guarded page-write path while retaining this PR's imported-source retry and bridge sync coalescing.
- **What did NOT change:** Out of scope and unchanged: no channel delivery, provider routing, plugin-hook contract, gateway method signature, config schema/default, or broad session model change; the behavior change is only the `extensions/memory-wiki` imported-source retry/coalescing path.
- Why it matters / User impact: concurrent memory-wiki bridge imports no longer duplicate expensive import passes or fail the bridge surface on transient filesystem `path-mismatch` races, without weakening path safety.

Related to #91154.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bridge-mode memory-wiki imported-source sync runs through the real OpenClaw gateway surface for `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace`; concurrent bridge calls for the same vault/config coalesce to one underlying bridge ingest/index-refresh pass; transient source-page rewrite pressure does not break the gateway or leave the bridge vault inconsistent.

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

I did not rerun the reporter-scale ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload, external channel delivery, or third-party provider/API proof on this head. This gateway proof pass also did not rerun the focused Vitest suite; the fresh proof above is runtime gateway evidence only.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 [P1] exact-head real behavior proof for bridge gateway methods and retry/coalescing behavior:** Addressed for the real gateway surface on exact head `30688580f1834a59895b987e69de44b2d8ec5bdd`. `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace` all succeeded against bridge mode with a real public memory artifact; the concurrent six-call probe produced exactly one new ingest entry. Remaining gap: the live rewrite-pressure probe did not naturally surface a `path-mismatch` log/error signal, so that part is disclosed instead of overstated.
- **RF-002 [P1] live/local bridge proof gap:** Addressed with an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway, memory-core + memory-wiki loaded, `vaultMode=bridge`, `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts=true`, and `bridgePublicArtifactCount=1` from an actual workspace `MEMORY.md` artifact.
- **RF-003 [P1] session-state / coalescing identity risk:** Addressed by the implementation and runtime probe. The coalescing key includes vault path/mode, bridge/ingest/render/search/context/obsidian config, and agent default/list workspace identity; the runtime concurrent batch updated the live artifact once and produced a single ingest delta across six gateway calls.
- **RF-004 [P1] stale gateway-load / reporter-scale proof:** Disclosed as unavailable in this environment. This update does not claim the reporter's ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload was rerun; it supplies exact-head local gateway proof for the memory-wiki bridge surface instead.
- **RF-005 [maintainer decision] merge-risk / canonical retry acceptance:** Still requires maintainer judgment. This rebase keeps current main's shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing; maintainers should make the final broad-vs-narrow canonical merge decision.
- **RF-006 [signal] fresh proof / re-review:** This update replaces stale pre-rebase proof with current-head runtime gateway evidence and records it through the daily-fix verification marker. The remaining proof gaps are explicitly listed in `What was not tested` rather than hidden behind local tests.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- ClawSweeper previously flagged overlap with #94443 on transient `path-mismatch` retry behavior.
- This conflict resolution uses the current main shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` retry behavior for the guarded write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing.
- This avoids restoring a divergent direct write retry path, but it does not override the remaining maintainer choice about broad-vs-narrow canonical merge direction.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts`; fresh maintainer proof for this update is the gateway runtime evidence above, not a test run.
- **Scenario locked in:** coalesced concurrent imported-source sync for identical bridge config, separate coalescing identity when workspace inputs differ, transient imported-source `path-mismatch` retry, preserved human Notes, and preserved symlink/path-alias + directory-collision refusal.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** these tests and the runtime gateway proof exercise the memory-wiki import/sync owner boundary that calls `syncImportedSourcesIfNeeded`; they avoid coupling the guardrail to unrelated channel delivery, provider routing, or UI behavior.

## Origin / follow-up

Existing PR tied to #91154. This update rebases the existing PR onto local `origin/main` ref `258b83c4386cdaf2cee0d64af64d20bb09443347`, resolves the source-page conflict, and revalidates exact head `30688580f1834a59895b987e69de44b2d8ec5bdd` through the local gateway surface.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`, `extensions: memory-wiki`.
- **Risk explanation:** Behavior change is limited to memory-wiki import/sync coalescing and imported source-page retry; concurrent callers now share one underlying bridge import/index-refresh pass for the same resolved config identity.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is confined to `extensions/memory-wiki`, coalescing identity includes the bridge artifact-discovery inputs that can change imported source results, and the runtime gateway proof shows repeated/concurrent bridge calls produce one consistent bridge source page and no warnings. Existing symlink/path-alias safety remains outside the retry path.
- **Remaining maintainer decision:** Accept whether this focused imported-source retry/coalescing patch is the desired canonical merge path alongside the broader guarded write behavior already present on main.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Concurrent bridge imported-source syncs for the same vault/config each performed independent artifact-discovery + import/index-refresh passes, and imported source-page stat/read/write treated transient fs-safe `path-mismatch` races as fatal.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix coalesces at the import/sync source boundary, where bridge artifact discovery and index refresh are owned, and adds bounded retry only for the identified transient filesystem condition rather than masking downstream failures or weakening path safety.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium-high: the exact-head gateway proof covers the bridge surface and concurrent coalescing behavior; confidence is bounded by the disclosed missing natural `path-mismatch` signal and missing reporter-scale WSL2/RSS workload.
- **Patch quality notes:** No skipped-test or lint suppression claims; no broad refactor. The catch/default paths are narrow guard behavior: `path-mismatch` is rethrown into the bounded retry loop, `not-found`/race reads are treated as no preservable existing notes, and the actual write remains guarded by `writeGuardedVaultPage`, so symlink/path-alias safety is not masked.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Source-of-truth boundary: `source-sync.ts` and `bridge.ts` own bridge artifact discovery, import, and index refresh; `source-page-shared.ts` owns imported source-page retry; `writeGuardedVaultPage` remains the canonical guarded vault write contract from main. Gateway methods are callers of this owner path, not new contract owners.

target.title: fix(tls): add subjectAltName to auto-generated gateway self-signed certificate (fixes #96910)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #96910.

When gateway TLS is enabled with `autoGenerate=true`, the self-signed certificate had no `subjectAltName` extension. Node.js ≥17 ignores the CN for hostname/IP verification per RFC 6125, causing CLI probe to `wss://127.0.0.1:18789` to fail.

## Changes Made

- New certs: Added `-addext subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,DNS:<hostname>,IP:127.0.0.1,IP:::1` to the openssl command
- Existing certs: Auto-detect CN-only certs (`CN=openclaw-gateway`, no SAN) and regenerate with SANs
- Transactional upgrade: old files renamed to `.bak`, restored on failure
- Custom certs (non-OpenClaw CN) are never touched

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts` — 10/10 passed

## Real behavior proof

```
# New cert: SAN verified via openssl
$ openssl x509 -in gateway-cert.pem -noout -ext subjectAltName
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
    DNS:localhost, DNS:LIN-66D8BD4EA2C, IP Address:127.0.0.1, IP Address:0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1

# Strict TLS check passes
$ node -e "tls.checkServerIdentity('127.0.0.1', cert)"
✅ STRICT TLS CHECK PASSED for 127.0.0.1

# Upgrade path: CN-only cert auto-detected and regenerated
[warn] gateway tls: upgrading CN-only certificate to include subjectAltName
[info] gateway tls: generated self-signed cert at ...

# Custom cert not touched
BEFORE: CN=custom-server, no SAN
AFTER:  CN=custom-server, no SAN (unchanged)
```

- ✅ New certs include subjectAltName
- ✅ Strict TLS identity check passes for IP and hostname
- ✅ Existing CN-only certs auto-upgraded with transactional backup/rollback
- ✅ Custom certificates (non-OpenClaw) are never rewritten

- [x] AI-assisted
